I thought to make a bit of a "less-technical" post today and reflect on the relationship between alcohol and our spirit (no pun intended), through the growth of one of the best characters from one of the best movies ever made: Andy Dufresne in The Shawshank Redemption.

It also gives me an excuse to post an awesome scene from the movie, here.

For the few who might not have seen the movie, what I'm posting does not contain spoilers, including the scene linked above.

Essentially, we know that Andy lands a life sentence in Shawshank Prison because of a bad experience with alcohol; whether or not he killed his wife is irrelevant, as his drunkenness puts him at the scene of the crime.

The flip side to this is that Andy quits booze, even when legitimately allowed to imbibe, as in the scene I linked. It's clear he has had time to understand his relationship with alcohol and with that understanding, in my opinion, comes a peace within him, allowing to reclaim the humanity which he had lost as a banker that drove his wife into the arms of another man (and, indirectly, caused her death).

Sure, it's just a movie, though what are movies but an exaggeration on the human experience. We're not all going to be served a life sentence for a mistake made while drinking, nor are we all going to refuse a cold beer with mates on a hot day while working, but what's important is that we understand the true nature of our own relationship with alcohol and act accordingly with our spirit.

For me, quitting alcohol has also put me at a kind of peace, and sectioning-off the habit from the other parts of my life, has allowed me to understand my relationship with drinking. Now, I'm beginning to change in a few ways and acting on it. Apart from becoming more emotional, I understand that I was deliberately (albeit, unconsciously), limiting my potential because I didn't feel I deserved better, so now I'm starting to pursue what I really want.

If you'd like to share how you understand your own relationship with drinking and how quitting, or reducing intake, is making a positive change in your life now, it would be nice to read about it.
